parts.label: Part 1
parts.title: Katsushika Hokusai
parts.article:
Katsushika Hokusai

(A) Hokusai (born October 1760, Edo [now Tokyo], Japan--died May 10, 1848) was a Japanese master artist and printmaker of the ukiyo-e ("pictures of the floating world") school. His early works represent the full spectrum of ukiyo-e art, including single-sheet prints of landscapes and screens, hand paintings, and surimono ("printed things"), such as greetings and announcements. Later he concentrated on the classical themes of the samurai and Chinese subjects. His famous print series "Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji," published between 1825 and 1833, marked the summit in the history of the Japanese landscape print.

Early years

(B) Hokusai was born in Edo. He was reportedly connected with the Nakajima family, though he was not accepted as the true son of Nakajima and was believed to have been born to a concubine. He became interested in drawing at an early age and was possibly supported by a prestigious artisan family.

(C) Hokusai is said to have served in his youth as a clerk in a lending bookshop, and from 15 to 18 years of age he was apprenticed to a wood-block engraver. This early training in the book and printing trades obviously contributed to Hokusai’s artistic development as a printmaker.

(D) The earliest contemporary record of Hokusai dates from the year 1778, when, at the age of 18, he became a pupil of the leading ukiyo-e master, Katsukawa Shunshō. The young Hokusai’s first published works appeared the following year--actor prints of the kabuki theatre, the genre that Shunshō and the Katsukawa school practically dominated.

(E) To judge from the ages of his several children, Hokusai must have married in his mid-20s. Possibly under the influence of family life, from this period his designs tended to turn from prints of actors and women to historical and landscape subjects, especially uki-e (semi-historical landscapes using Western-influenced perspective techniques), as well as prints of children. The artist’s book illustrations and texts turned as well from the earlier themes to historical and didactic subjects. At the same time, Hokusai’s work in the surimono genre during the subsequent decade marks one of the early peaks in his career. Surimono were prints issued privately for special occasions--New Year’s and other greetings, musical programs and announcements, private verse selections--in limited editions and featuring immaculate printing of the highest quality.

Middle years

(F) In his middle years, Hokusai experienced significant artistic evolution and personal hardship. He began to distance himself from the Katsukawa school, partly due to the death of his master Shunshō in 1792 and partly due to his own burgeoning interest in other Japanese and Chinese artistic traditions. He started using the name "Hokusai" around 1797, and his work from this period shows a broader range of influences.

(G) A series of personal tragedies, including the death of his wife and his own financial struggles, seemed to fuel rather than hinder his artistic output. He moved residences frequently--some accounts say over ninety times in his life--often to avoid creditors. Despite this instability, the period from 1800 to 1820 was one of prodigious production. He created several major illustrated books, including the first volumes of his instructional manga (random drawings), which were sketchbooks of countless subjects--animals, people, mythological figures--intended as model books for other artists. These manga volumes became widely popular and demonstrated his incredible draftsmanship and observational skill.

Later years and legacy

(H) Hokusai’s most celebrated work was created in his seventies. It was during this period that he produced the iconic "Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji," which includes the world-renowned print "The Great Wave off Kanagawa." This series was revolutionary for its bold composition, innovative use of the newly affordable Prussian blue pigment, and its focus on the daily lives of common people within dramatic landscapes. The series was so popular that ten additional prints were added to the original thirty-six.

(I) In his later writings, Hokusai expressed a profound belief in his own artistic growth with age. He famously wrote that by the age of 110, every dot and line he drew would be alive. Though he never reached that age, he continued working relentlessly until his death at 88. Hokusai’s influence extended far beyond Japan; after the country opened up in the Meiji period, his prints reached Europe and profoundly impacted the Impressionist and Art Nouveau movements. Artists like Claude Monet and Vincent van Gogh collected his prints and were inspired by his compositions and use of color.

questions.question: Hokusai’s series "Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji" was published over an eight-year period.

analyses.content: 1825年到1833年刚好跨越了8年的时间，这和题目说的“历时8年”完全一致。
你可能在找原文里有没有直接写数字“8”，但遇到年份范围时一定要自己动笔减一下才能发现正确对应关系。
"His famous print series "Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji," published between 1825 and 1833, marked the summit in the history of the Japanese landscape print."

questions.question: Hokusai was the biological son of the Nakajima family.

analyses.content: 原文明确说他“没有被接纳为真正的儿子（not accepted as the true son）”，这就直接反驳了题目里“亲生儿子（biological son）”的说法。
你可能看到前半句“和中岛家族有联系”就匆忙选了TRUE，做题时必须把带有转折词（though）的后半句读完。
"He was reportedly connected with the Nakajima family, though he was not accepted as the true son of Nakajima and was believed to have been born to a concubine."

questions.question: Hokusai’s apprenticeship with a wood-block engraver lasted for four years.

analyses.content: 从15岁到18岁做学徒，时间跨度应该是3年，而不是题目里宣称的4年。
你可能在脑子里掰手指把15、16、17、18数成了四个年头，但计算时间跨度直接用18减去15即可。
"Hokusai is said to have served in his youth as a clerk in a lending bookshop, and from 15 to 18 years of age he was apprenticed to a wood-block engraver."

questions.question: Hokusai’s first published works were landscapes.

analyses.content: 原文白纸黑字写着他最初发表的作品是“演员版画（actor prints）”，这跟题目里说的“风景画（landscapes）”对不上。
你可能会凭着对这位画家是“风景画大师”的刻板印象直接选对，但阅读理解只能依靠原文信息来判断他“第一次”的作品类型。

"(D) The earliest contemporary record of Hokusai dates from the year 1778, when, at the age of 18, he became a pupil of the leading ukiyo-e master, Katsukawa Shunshō. The young Hokusai’s first published works appeared the following year--actor prints of the kabuki theatre, the genre that Shunshō and the Katsukawa school practically dominated."

questions.question: Hokusai’s work in the surimono genre is considered one of the early high points of his career.

analyses.content: 原文用“早期的顶峰（early peaks）”来形容这个阶段，完美等同于题目里的“早期的最高点（early high points）”。
你可能会因为不认识“surimono”这个生僻词就放弃这道题，但只要按图索骥去匹配后面的“peaks”和“high points”就能拿分。

"At the same time, Hokusai’s work in the surimono genre during the subsequent decade marks one of the early peaks in his career. Surimono were prints issued privately for special occasions--New Year’s and other greetings, musical programs and announcements, private verse selections--in limited editions and featuring immaculate printing of the highest quality."

questions.question: The death of his master Shunshō was the only reason Hokusai distanced himself from the Katsukawa school.

analyses.content: 师傅去世只是他离开门派的“部分原因（partly due to）”，原文还提到他对其他艺术产生了兴趣，所以并非如题目所说是“唯一原因（only reason）”。
只要在题目里看到“唯一（only）”这种非常绝对的词，你就要高度警惕，回原文检查是不是还有其他并列的原因。

"He began to distance himself from the Katsukawa school, partly due to the death of his master Shunshō in 1792 and partly due to his own burgeoning interest in other Japanese and Chinese artistic traditions."

analyses.content: 顺着题目里“做店员（clerk in a...）”这个线索找，原文在clerk后面紧跟着地点就是“lending bookshop”。
你可能只填了“bookshop”，虽然意思差不多，但在字数限制内填上修饰词“lending”才能确保答案最精确。
"Hokusai is said to have served in his youth as a clerk in a lending bookshop, and from 15 to 18 years of age he was apprenticed to a wood-block engraver."
题目问他15到18岁时被送去给谁当学徒（apprenticed to a...），原文对应的正是“wood-block engraver”。
这个答案带有连字符，你可能会犹豫要不要拆开，直接把这一整个名词词组照抄进答题卡就不会出错。
"Hokusai is said to have served in his youth as a clerk in a lending bookshop, and from 15 to 18 years of age he was apprenticed to a wood-block engraver."
题目想知道哪种题材使用了西方透视法（Western perspective），原文括号里的解释直接绑定了目标词“uki-e”。
你可能会抄前面范围更大的“landscape subjects”，但括号里的具体解释只针对“uki-e”，填最具体的名词才对。

"(E) To judge from the ages of his several children, Hokusai must have married in his mid-20s. Possibly under the influence of family life, from this period his designs tended to turn from prints of actors and women to historical and landscape subjects, especially uki-e (semi-historical landscapes using Western-influenced perspective techniques), as well as prints of children."
题目问什么东西有着高质量（high-quality），原文的“highest quality”前面用来修饰的词正是“printing”。
你可能在一个很长的句子里看花了眼，这时候只要牢牢盯住题目里的“high-quality”去对应原文的“highest quality”，答案就在前面。

"Surimono were prints issued privately for special occasions--New Year’s and other greetings, musical programs and announcements, private verse selections--in limited editions and featuring immaculate printing of the highest quality."
题目问他在大约什么时间开始用“Hokusai”这个名字，原文极其直白地写着“around 1797”。
这就是一道简单的数字扫读题，你只要在原文中定位人名和代表大约的“around”，就能毫无悬念地拿到分数。
"He started using the name "Hokusai" around 1797, and his work from this period shows a broader range of influences."
题目寻找的是等同于艺术家速写本（sketchbooks）的出版物，原文明确说明“instructional manga”就是这种速写本。
你可能会填括号里的“random drawings”，但这只是解释，真正的核心出版物名称是它前面的“instructional manga”。

"He created several major illustrated books, including the first volumes of his instructional manga (random drawings), which were sketchbooks of countless subjects--animals, people, mythological figures--intended as model books for other artists."
题目问这个系列使用了一种什么名字的新型蓝色颜料（blue pigment），原文一模一样的地方写着“Prussian blue”。
你很容易就能定位到颜料名称，但千万别忘了“Prussian”是一个专有名词，填答题卡时必须要保留大写。

"It was during this period that he produced the iconic "Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji," which includes the world-renowned print "The Great Wave off Kanagawa." This series was revolutionary for its bold composition, innovative use of the newly affordable Prussian blue pigment, and its focus on the daily lives of common people within dramatic landscapes."

groups.description: Choose NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS from the passage for each answer.
